1.explanation: The PageHeader component renders the title by delegating to the Heading component (imported from Heading.js), so any wrapping behavior must be implemented in the StyledHeading CSS. The StyledHeading styled component controls the text format via the sizeStyle helper, which sets the max-width and line-height but does not enable word wrapping or breaking for unbroken strings. To fix the overflow issue, the StyledHeading (or its sizeStyle) needs to include CSS properties such as word-break or overflow-wrap so that long, punctuation-only strings can break rather than overflow.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows a PageHeader with a very long title string (“LVL3928734.haiku.yosemite_342397”) that runs off the right edge of its container and overlaps the action button instead of wrapping onto the next line. Because there are no natural whitespace breaks in the string, the heading overflows and collides with adjacent content rather than breaking or wrapping within its allotted grid area.

2.explanation: The PageHeader component renders its title via the Heading component, which under the hood uses StyledHeading. In StyledHeading, the sizeStyle function applies a fixed max-width based on theme values but does not enable wrapping for long, unbroken words. Additionally, the truncateStyle CSS enforces white-space: nowrap when the truncate prop is used (though not in this case), indicating where wrapping behavior is controlled. Because there is no overflow-wrap or word-break rule, any single, continuous string longer than the max-width simply spills out of its container. To fix the overflow, adjustments must be made in StyledHeading (for example, adding overflow-wrap: break-word or word-break: break-all, or allowing fillProp by default) so that long headings wrap as intended within PageHeader.
2.bug_scenario: A very long, unbroken heading string passed to PageHeader is not wrapping within its container. Instead, it overflows horizontally and collides with adjacent elements (e.g. the action button) rather than breaking onto multiple lines as expected.
